notes: In his latest memo, Howard Marks writes that the investment world may be experiencing the third major sea change over the last 50 years. Events in recent years – especially the spike in inflation and the Federal Reserve’s response – appear to have caused a reversal of the market conditions that prevailed during the post-GFC (Global Financial Crisis) period and for much of the last four decades. Howard discusses what this potentially new era could mean for lenders, especially bargain hunters.  The memo is read by LJ Ganser. You can read the memo here (https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/sea-change).

thesis: The speaker identifies two historical sea changes in investing: the shift in the mid-1970s toward a risk-return mindset that enabled high-yield bonds and private equity, and the subsequent four-decade decline in interest rates driven by Paul Volker's control of inflation. He argues that this combination of factors, particularly the massive drop in interest rates, created an incredible tailwind that fueled economic growth, corporate profitability, and a compound annual stock market return of 10.3% per year.
